# archestra_chatops_slack (Resource)

The organization's Slack integration, so people can chat with agents in Slack. One per organization; to give an agent its own Slack bot, use `archestra_chatops_slack_agent_bot`. Secrets are write-only: the API never returns them, so a change made outside Terraform is not detected. Destroying the resource turns the integration off and keeps the stored credentials. Enabling it checks the bot token with Slack.

## Example Usage

```terraform
variable "slack_bot_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "slack_app_level_token" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

resource "archestra_chatops_slack" "this" {
  connection_mode = "socket"
  app_id          = "A0123456789"
  bot_token       = var.slack_bot_token
  app_level_token = var.slack_app_level_token
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `app_id` (String) Slack app ID.
- `app_level_token` (String, Sensitive) Slack app-level token (`xapp-…`), used in socket mode.
- `bot_token` (String, Sensitive) Slack bot token (`xoxb-…`).
- `connection_mode` (String) How Slack reaches Archestra: `socket` or `webhook`.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the integration is on.
- `signing_secret` (String, Sensitive) Slack signing secret, used in webhook mode.

### Read-Only

- `configured` (Boolean) Whether the stored configuration is complete.
- `id` (String) Integration name.
- `updated_at` (String) Time the configuration was last saved.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import archestra_chatops_slack.this slack
```
